newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra signs airline code-share agreement.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra signs airline code-share agreement.

text.p: Australian airline passengers would know when they were flying on a code-share service under a government agreement with the major airlines and the travel industry, Transport Minister John Sharp said on Thursday.

The government's code of conduct agreement with Qantas Airways Ltd, Ansett Australia and the Australian Federation of Travel Agents would ensure that tickets would be clearly marked if it was a code-share service and that passengers received printed information of that fact.
Under a code-share agreement, a carrier sells seats on another airline's services as if they are its own.
Code-share flights were also to be clearly marked on airline timetables, Sharp said in a statement.
"This is a first step in improving the information available to airline consumers and endorses a key finding of the Plane Safe report released late last year," Sharp said.
Sharp also released a new annual publication, Aviation Safety Indicators, to help consumers' awareness of the health of the aviation industry.
From January, the government would publish monthly bulletins of any serious deficiencies in airlines and would name them.
"This will be a very big incentive for the airlines to maintain the regulations at all times otherwise they'll get bad publicity," Sharp said.
